what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved a waiver reducing the required distance between buildings in the White Woods development, then approved the overall modification.
The board approved the overall modification to the White Woods plan and closed the public hearing.
The board reorganized: Joanna Ballotta was chosen as chair and Damon McQuaid as clerk; the vice chair vote was not audible in the captions.
The June 24th meeting was replaced by a regular meeting on the 18th focused on board goals, and goals and policies go on the next agenda.
The planning director's report noted the town receives a payment per unit as occupancy permits issue under the 40R district, and received a state grant when it was created.

why_it_matters: The White Woods approval changes how close buildings can sit in a residential development, which affects neighbors and the density of the project.
The 40R payments are money that comes to the town budget, mostly taxes, as units are occupied, so housing built in the district can add revenue over time.
watch_next: The regular meeting on the 18th, replacing June 24th, which is set to take up board goals and policies.
